nodes.label: desktop memory - what herb-eval is, and why herb is contaminated

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. herb-eval is the prior v1 and thesis artefact build under the superseded design - a contrast and forensic baseline, not the v3 artefact. The framing of herb as the full DB and herb-eval as the eval-safe copy is wrong: herb has the answerable_questions, unanswerable_questions and oracle product_profile sections ingested, which is contaminated state from an ingestion error, and those QA and oracle sections are the gold answers, so their presence makes any retrieval or statistic read from herb misleading. For any live-graph query, distribution, count or eval, target herb-eval only; Chunk.section in {answerable_questions, unanswerable_questions, product_profile} is the contamination marker and those rows do not exist in herb-eval. Sharpened 2026-06-12: the v1 build chunked AND tagged the full oracle - 815 answerable with ground_truth and citation copies, and 699 unanswerable - both fed to the tagger as knowledge, and herb-eval is a filter, not a rebuild, excluding those chunks but preserving chunk descriptions, relevance scores and tag weights produced by the contaminated tagging run, re-embedding tags as the only mitigation, so second-order residue was filtered around and never eliminated. Confirmed 2026-06-15 by live read-only inventory: herb-eval has 0 oracle chunks and 0 orphan tags, at 4,869 chunks / 33 files / 24,804 tags, so the oracle chunk removal is done and what the filter left is the model-output residue. CANON_AUDIT.md 6.7 flags the sibling claim in v3-artefact-subsystem.md that herb-eval is never queried live as STALE
